note: Both sets capture the core Nitinol material and phase-transformation facts accurately and with supporting quotes. Set B additionally extracts the second commercially available wire transition temperature (90 C), which the footnote states ('transition at temperatures of 70C and 90C'), while Set A only captures 70 C and so omits an important value. Otherwise the two sets are essentially identical in binding, conditions and quotes.
remarks: Both sets share a slightly reworded quote for the 'material composition | nickel-titanium alloy' claim (the source reads 'The actuation, or contraction, of the Nitinol wire is a solid-state phase transformation based on atomic-level characteristic of the nickel-titanium alloy'); the claim itself is supported, so this is minor. Note the page's stated composition ranges (55-65% Ni and 44-55% Ti) sum to more than 100% — an internal inconsistency in the source, faithfully reproduced by both sets. Facts on the page neither set shows include the 1961 discovery of Nitinol and the 1930s start of SMA research (dates, largely administrative/historical).
